corrections.issue: Wrong speaker: the legal offering-document cap, the 70% losing trades statement and the canola versus 5-year note comparison are Moritz Seibert describing his own fund (Drew's Tactical had already closed).
corrections.fix: Seibert caps his fund's size in the offering documents so it can keep trading small markets such as lumber, oats and canola; individual trades in these markets lose about 70% of the time, but adding canola to the 10-year note helps the portfolio much more than adding the 5-year note.

corrections.issue: Wrong speaker and claim: the liquidity and key-person argument (monthly liquidity, no 3-year swap exit) is Moritz Seibert's reasoning in his question; Drew's own answer was that investors were understanding when Tactical closed in early 2023 after two long-time key employees retired.
corrections.fix: Seibert argues that a liquid futures manager can return capital within 30 days, so a closure is a small event compared with illiquid strategies; Drew replies that Tactical closed in 2023 when two key employees retired, and that investors understood.

completeness_estimate: 0.80 - first reader caught the central hedger-premium method, three-part system framework, portfolio orthogonality and business-model points; missed several supporting reasoning steps and two speaker attributions were wrong.
